title: Auth and access plane
subtitle: How commercial AI assistants and my own agents reach a private tool estate: OAuth, token validation, edge exposure and an operations layer

stats.label: approves every grant on the consent screen
tools: the full local surface, and the trimmed one shown to Copilot Studio
token issuers the gateway accepts: my server and Microsoft's platform

lede: My tool estate is private, and I wanted commercial AI assistants, including Microsoft Copilot Studio, to connect to it on my terms, alongside my own agents. The access plane is how they get in: an OAuth authorization server, gateway token validation against several issuers, an edge proxy that exposes a trimmed tool surface to a vendor's agent platform, and an operations layer that runs the estate. The consent screen is the control. Assistants self-register as OAuth clients, and a human approves each grant. A security review once found anonymous registration with attacker-chosen redirects, I locked registration down, and the next morning every assistant was locked out.
quote: The lock looked like security; the consent step is security, because a human sees exactly which client is asking for exactly what.
evidence: OAuth 2.0 and identity architecture: commercial AI assistants and my own agents admitted to a private tool estate as OAuth clients, with 1 person approving every grant on the consent screen.
Delegated authorization for AI agents: one gateway that accepts tokens from 2 issuers, my own authorization server and Microsoft's platform, before any tool is visible.
Microsoft Copilot Studio integration: an edge proxy that shows Copilot Studio a trimmed surface of 8 tools out of the 21 on the local surface, without opening the estate behind it.
Zero-trust and zero-inbound networking: a private tool estate reached by commercial assistants with no open inbound ports.
Security judgment under operational load: consent chosen over registration as the control point, and my own registration lock reverted the day after I added it.
author: Corey James
